app.lema: Optimize images with the Squoosh engines

estudio.soltarDetalle: PNG, JPEG, HEIC (iPhone), AVIF, JPEG XL, WebP, TIFF, GIF, BMP, QOI or PNM
estudio.avisoOrientacion: This photo has an orientation in its metadata: without auto-rotating it, the result comes out rotated, just like with cwebp.

comparador.etiqueta: Comparison of the original and the result
comparador.otraProporcion: The result has a different aspect ratio: they're shown side by side.
comparador.reducida: View scaled to {{porcentaje}}%: click here to see it at 100%, with more detail
comparador.recorteRotulo: Crop · {{ancho}} × {{alto}} px · drag the frame or its corners

orden.pegar: Paste a cwebp, cjpeg, oxipng, qoiconv, avifenc or cjxl command

motivo.enderezada: The photo is auto-rotated, and {{herramienta}} doesn't rotate photos: this command doesn't produce exactly this file.
motivo.procesada: Apolo cropped it, resized it or reduced its palette first: {{herramienta}} doesn't do it the same way, and this command doesn't produce this file.
motivo.formato_sin_herramienta: {{herramienta}} can't read {{formato}}: the command works as a reference, but it can't be run as is.

panel.izquierdaOriginal: The original is on the left. You can put another format there to compare two results with each other, for example WebP against JPEG.
panel.sinOpciones: {{formato}} has no options: there's only one way to encode it, lossless.

porQue.sinAlfa: The image has no transparency, or it's discarded.
porQue.conZopfli: With Zopfli, Zopfli does the compression.
porQue.jpegSinPerdida: cjxl recompresses this JPEG losslessly: turn off “Recompress the JPEG losslessly” to choose the quality.
porQue.soloJpeg: Only applies if the input image is a JPEG.
porQue.sinCalidad: This format has no quality to search for (lossless).
porQue.laBuscaApolo: Apolo searches for it to reach the score.

opcion.calidadAyuda: Higher means more faithful and bigger. Around 75–85 is usually invisible to the naked eye.
opcion.esfuerzoAyuda: Lossless, the image always comes out identical: more effort is slower and a bit smaller.
opcion.sinPerdidaAyuda: Every pixel comes out exact. For screenshots, graphics and logos; on photos it's much bigger.
opcion.enderezarAyuda: Rotates the photo as its EXIF orientation says, before anything else. No tool does this: with it on, the command no longer produces the same file.
opcion.nivelSinPerdidaAyuda: A shortcut that sets method and effort at once, from 0 (fast) to 9 (slow and smaller).
opcion.metodoAyuda: How hard the compressor searches for the best way to encode each block. 6 is the smallest and the slowest.
opcion.casiSinPerdidaAyuda: Tweaks the pixels slightly so it's smaller without it showing. 100 is off; 60 already saves quite a lot.
opcion.tamanoObjetivoAyuda: Searches for the quality that gives this size. 0 is off. It makes several passes: slower.
opcion.yuvNitidoAyuda: A more careful color conversion: cleaner color edges (red text, thin lines), a bit slower.
opcion.autofiltroAyuda: Adjusts the deblocking filter strength for each image on its own.
opcion.calidadAlfaAyuda: Below 100, the transparent edge is simplified and gets smaller.
opcion.exactoAyuda: Keeps the color under fully transparent pixels. It's usually thrown away, because it can't be seen.
opcion.mezclarAlfaAyuda: Blends the transparency with this color, as if the image were on top of it.
opcion.modoRedimensionAyuda: Only shrink avoids enlarging images that are already small.
opcion.metadatosAyuda: EXIF holds the camera, the date and sometimes the location; ICC, the color profile; XMP, rights and editing.
opcion.segmentosAyuda: How many zones the image is split into to compress each one differently.
opcion.snsAyuda: How much it takes advantage of the eye seeing detail less well in textured areas.
opcion.fuerzaFiltroAyuda: Smooths the block edges. Higher means fewer blocks and softer.
opcion.filtroFuerteAyuda: A more aggressive filter than the simple one. On by default.
opcion.psnrObjetivoAyuda: Searches for the quality that gives this measured fidelity. 0 is off; 42 is very good.
opcion.pasadasAyuda: Analysis passes when there's a target size or PSNR.
opcion.rangoCalidadAyuda: Limits for the quality when searching for a size or a PSNR.
opcion.limiteParticionAyuda: Only for huge images that don't fit in the format: lowers the quality just enough.
opcion.compresionAlfaAyuda: Uncompressed only makes sense for comparing.
opcion.filtradoAlfaAyuda: Best searches for the filter that saves the most on the alpha channel.
opcion.emularJpegAyuda: Adjusts the quality so the size resembles that of a JPEG at the same quality. Experimental.
opcion.preprocesadoAyuda: Prior smoothing by segments, or dithering. Experimental.
opcion.hilosAyuda: Uses more processor cores. The result is the same.
opcion.pocaMemoriaAyuda: For huge images: uses less memory and takes longer.
opcion.redimensionCwebpAyuda: cwebp's -resize, with its own method. To repeat a cwebp command; normally you'd use Resize under Processing, which works for every format.
opcion.recorteCwebpAyuda: cwebp's -crop. To repeat a cwebp command; normally you'd use Crop under Processing.
opcion.procesoRedimensionAyuda: Changes the size before compressing, in any format. Leave one side empty to keep the aspect ratio.
opcion.procesoRecorteAyuda: Keeps a rectangle of the image, before resizing.
opcion.procesoPaletaAyuda: Leaves the image with few colors using libimagequant, like Squoosh. Much smaller as PNG; dithering hides the color steps.
opcion.calidadJpegAyuda: Higher means more faithful and bigger. From 80, MozJPEG reduces color less, and from 90 not at all.
opcion.colorJpegAyuda: Gray removes color entirely. RGB keeps the color without converting it to YCbCr: bigger, and almost never needed.
opcion.escaneoJpegAyuda: Progressive shows the whole image, sharper and sharper, while it loads, and is usually smaller. Sequential loads from top to bottom.
opcion.afinadoJpegAyuda: Which quality metric the quantization is tuned to. PSNR-HVS is MozJPEG's and looks the best.
opcion.muestreoJpegAyuda: How much color is kept relative to brightness. 4:2:0 is smaller; 4:4:4 keeps color edges sharp, as in colored text.
opcion.tablaJpegAyuda: The base table that decides which detail is lost. Table 3, from ImageMagick, is MozJPEG's.
opcion.suavizadoJpegAyuda: Smooths the image before compressing: for images with dithering or noise. At 0, none.
opcion.sinTrellisJpegAyuda: Turns off MozJPEG's trellis quantization: faster and a bit bigger.
opcion.revertirJpegAyuda: The classic JPEG defaults, without MozJPEG's improvements. Bigger; for comparing.
opcion.rapidoJpegAyuda: Doesn't search for the best split of the progressive scans: faster and a bit bigger.
opcion.dcScanJpegAyuda: How the first progressive scan is grouped. It rarely changes anything.
opcion.dctJpegAyuda: Accurate integer is the classic one. Fast and floating point are older methods.
opcion.tablasBaselineJpegAyuda: Limits the tables to 8 bits, for very old readers.
opcion.sinOvershootJpegAyuda: Turns off MozJPEG's trick that removes halos around black text on white.
opcion.sinJfifJpegAyuda: Removes 18 bytes of header. Browsers read it just the same, but it's not quite standard.
opcion.optimizarJpegAyuda: Computes custom Huffman tables. MozJPEG already does it by default; it only changes anything with “Like libjpeg”.
opcion.nivelPngAyuda: How hard OxiPNG searches for the best compression. Higher is slower and a bit smaller. It never loses quality.
opcion.alfaPngAyuda: Changes the color of fully transparent pixels, which can't be seen, if that compresses better.
opcion.quitarPngAyuda: Safe strips what doesn't change how the image looks. All also strips the color profile.
opcion.entrelazadoPngAyuda: Interlaced shows the whole image while it loads, but it's bigger.
opcion.zopfliPngAyuda: A much slower compressor that squeezes out a bit more.
opcion.iteracionesPngAyuda: More iterations, slower and a little smaller. 15 if left empty.
opcion.compresionPngAyuda: The libdeflate level. By default the level decides.
opcion.rapidoPngAyuda: Chooses the filter with a quick estimate instead of actually compressing.
opcion.sinReduccionesPngAyuda: Doesn't change the bit depth, the color type or the palette; it only recompresses.
opcion.sinBitsPngAyuda: Doesn't lower the color depth even if it's more than needed.
opcion.sinColorPngAyuda: Doesn't go, for example, from RGB to a palette.
opcion.sinPaletaPngAyuda: Doesn't remove unused colors from the palette.
opcion.sinGrisPngAyuda: Doesn't convert a color image that only has grays to grayscale.
opcion.sinRecodificarPngAyuda: If there's no reduction, leaves the compressed data as it is.
opcion.escala16PngAyuda: Converts a 16-bit image to 8 bits, scaling. It loses some precision.
opcion.forzarPngAyuda: Writes the result even if it gains nothing over the original.
opcion.calidadAvifAyuda: Higher means more faithful and bigger. 100 is lossless. avifenc uses 60 if left alone.
opcion.velocidadAvifAyuda: Lower is slower and a bit smaller. 6 is avifenc's default; below 4 it can take a long time.
opcion.sinPerdidaAvifAyuda: The image comes out identical, in 4:4:4 and without converting the color. It's quite a lot bigger.
opcion.calidadAlfaAvifAyuda: The alpha channel's quality. If left alone, the same as the color's.
opcion.submuestreoAvifAyuda: 4:2:0 keeps the color at half resolution: it's smaller and barely noticeable in photos. 4:4:4 keeps all of it.
opcion.sharpyuvAvifAyuda: A slower conversion to 4:2:0 that avoids muddy color edges.
opcion.afinadoAvifAyuda: The metric aom tries to improve. IQ, the default for still images, aims at what the eye sees.
opcion.nitidezAvifAyuda: Prefers keeping edges sharp when distributing the bits (0 to 7).
opcion.progresivoAvifAyuda: Stores a quick version before the full one, so it shows while it loads. A bit bigger.
opcion.profundidadAvifAyuda: 10 or 12 bits give finer gradients and are a bit bigger. By default, the input's.
opcion.rangoLimitadoAvifAyuda: The video range (16–235) instead of the full one. Only for very specific cases.
opcion.premultiplicarAvifAyuda: Stores the color already multiplied by the transparency.
opcion.sinExifAvifAyuda: Doesn't copy the camera data (date, location, orientation).
opcion.sinIccAvifAyuda: Doesn't copy the ICC profile. Colors may change if it wasn't sRGB.
opcion.calidadJxlAyuda: 90 is “visually lossless”, cjxl's default. 100 is lossless.
opcion.esfuerzoJxlAyuda: Higher is slower and a bit smaller. 7 is cjxl's default.
opcion.jpegSinPerdidaJxlAyuda: Stores the same JPEG in less space, and it can be recovered byte for byte. Off, it encodes its pixels at the chosen quality.
opcion.distanciaAlfaJxlAyuda: 0 stores the alpha channel losslessly, cjxl's default. 1 is “visually lossless”.
opcion.progresivoJxlAyuda: Shows sooner while it loads. A bit bigger.
opcion.modularJxlAyuda: VarDCT is for photos; modular, for graphics and lossless. By default cjxl chooses.
opcion.ruidoJxlAyuda: Adds, when decoding, grain like a photo at that ISO: 100 is a little, 3200 a lot. Empty, no grain.
opcion.epfJxlAyuda: The strength of the filter that smooths without blurring edges. By default cjxl chooses.
opcion.gaborishJxlAyuda: A filter that hides the blocks. By default cjxl chooses.
opcion.decodificacionRapidaJxlAyuda: Higher opens sooner, at the cost of some quality or size.
opcion.notaObjetivoAyuda: Apolo tries qualities and keeps the lowest one that reaches this SSIMULACRA 2 score. The command carries the quality found. It takes several tries.

quitarPng.seguro: The ones that can't be seen

lotes.soltarDetalle: They're all converted with the same preset, including those in subfolders. The originals aren't touched.
lotes.sinRutasNavegador: The browser doesn't say which folder what you drop comes from: type the path below.
lotes.ninguna: There's no image here that Apolo can open.
lotes.nuncaPisa: The source subfolders are repeated inside. If a file already exists, the new one gets a number after it: nothing is ever overwritten.
lotes.mayores_one: 1 image is bigger than its original. It was saved anyway: it's in the list below.
lotes.mayores_other: {{count}} images are bigger than their originals. They were saved anyway: they're in the list below.
lotes.fallidas_one: 1 image couldn't be converted: the reason is in the list.
lotes.fallidas_other: {{count}} images couldn't be converted: the reason is in the list.
lotes.peores: The ones that save the least
lotes.peoresDetalle: If any come out almost the same or bigger, they may have been well compressed already, or another preset may suit them better.
lotes.masLigero: Save only the lightest of each image
lotes.masLigeroDetalle: A single file is saved for each image: the format that weighs the least.
lotes.todosDetalle: One file per format is saved for each image.
lotes.medirDetalle: Each image gets its SSIMULACRA 2 score, and the summary points out the ones with the worst score. The batch takes longer.
lotes.objetivo: Search for the quality by score
lotes.objetivoDetalle: For each image, the lowest quality that reaches the score, in the lossy formats. It makes several tries per image: it takes quite a bit longer.
lotes.peoresNotas: The ones with the worst score
lotes.peoresNotasDetalle: The ones that stray furthest from their original.

ajustes.licencia: Free software under the GPLv3 license.
ajustes.avisarme: Let me know when there's a new version
ajustes.privacidad: It's the only thing Apolo does outside your computer: once a day it asks GitHub for the latest published version. It doesn't send your images, who you are or how often you use it. GitHub sees your IP address, like any page you visit.
ajustes.idiomaDetalle: For Apolo's menus, notices and messages

pesos.barra: The result is {{porcentaje}}% of the original's size

presets.entradilla: A preset is a saved setting to use again: in the Studio, in batches or from the command line.
presets.comoCrear: They're created in the Studio: adjust an image and, in the panel on the right, type a name and press “Save”.
presets.donde: Each preset is a JSON file in this folder, shared with the command line; to move them to another computer, copy the file:

novedad.lista: Apolo {{version}} is ready. It will be installed and reopen.
novedad.instalando: Installing Apolo {{version}}. The window will close and reopen…
novedad.traslocada: To update itself, Apolo has to be in Applications: drag it there and open it from that folder

medidas.ayudaNota: How close it is to the original, as a person would see it: from 100 (identical) downwards. At 90 you can't tell them apart even flipping between them, at 80 not side by side, 70 is high quality.
medidas.ayudaTecnicas: PSNR (in decibels) and SSIM (from 0 to 1): the classic technical measures. Higher means closer.
medidas.noAlcanzada: Doesn't reach it even at quality 100
medidas.buscando: Searching for the quality for a score of {{nota}}…

agentes.subtitulo: Claude, Cursor, VS Code and the rest, over the MCP protocol.
agentes.seActualiza: It updates along with Apolo: there's nothing to reinstall.
agentes.reiniciarTitulo: After updating Apolo, quit and reopen Claude Desktop.
agentes.reiniciarTexto: Or turn the extension off and on in Claude Desktop › Settings › Extensions. In Claude Code, start a new session. Until then the agent keeps the previous version, and will tell you there's a new one.
agentes.avisoAppimage: From the AppImage there's no fixed path: it's mounted in a different folder every time. For agents, install the .deb or download the command-line package, which includes apolo-mcp.
agentes.avisoTraslocada: macOS is running Apolo from a temporary copy. Move it to Applications and reopen it to add it to an agent.
agentes.avisoNoEncontrado: This build of Apolo doesn't have apolo-mcp next to it.
agentes.desktopTexto: Create the extension and open it with a double click, or drag it to Claude Desktop › Settings › Extensions. It's installed once: it uses this Apolo's apolo-mcp, so it updates along with it (restarting Claude Desktop after updating).
agentes.cursor: Cursor and Claude Desktop by hand
agentes.cursorTexto: In ~/.cursor/mcp.json, or in the Claude Desktop configuration file:
agentes.vscodeTexto: In .vscode/mcp.json, or in your profile with “MCP: Add Server”. VS Code uses servers, and the rest, mcpServers.
agentes.queHaceTexto: Analyze images, optimize them, compare formats at the same quality, measure the loss, look at them, convert whole folders and use your presets. It always writes new files: Apolo never overwrites or deletes anything.
agentes.terminal: An agent with a terminal, like Claude Code, could move or delete files with its own tools: ask it to check with you first.
agentes.privacidadTexto: Apolo works on this computer and doesn't send anything anywhere. But what the agent asks for —paths, file names, the thumbnails it looks at— goes into its conversation, and the model provider sees that.
agentes.permiso: There's nothing to turn on: adding it to an agent gives it permission, and removing it from the agent takes it away.
